content: Title 21 of the United States Code is the section of federal law that regulates food and drugs. It is organized into 25 chapters, each addressing specific areas of regulation and oversight. Below are the chapters and their respective focus areas: 1. Adulterated or Misbranded Foods or Drugs: This chapter addresses the regulation and prohibition of food and drugs that are adulterated or misbranded, ensuring public safety and accurate labeling. 2. Teas (Repealed): This chapter previously dealt with regulations concerning teas but has since been repealed. 3. Filled Milk: This chapter governs the production and sale of filled milk, a product made by combining milk with fats or oils other than milk fat. 4. Animals, Meats, and Meat and Dairy Products: This chapter focuses on the regulation of animals, meat, and dairy products to ensure their safety and quality for human consumption. 5. Viruses, Serums, Toxins, Antitoxins, and Analogous Products: This chapter regulates biological products such as vaccines, serums, and antitoxins to ensure their safety, efficacy, and proper manufacturing. 6. Bureau of Narcotics (Omitted): This chapter, now omitted, previously addressed the Bureau of Narcotics. 7. Narcotic Drugs (Repealed or Transferred): This chapter previously dealt with narcotic drugs but has been repealed or its provisions transferred to other sections. 8. Practice of Pharmacy and Sale of Poisons in Consular Districts in China: This chapter historically regulated the practice of pharmacy and the sale of poisons in U.S. consular districts in China. 9. Narcotic Farms: This chapter pertains to the establishment and operation of narcotic farms for the treatment and rehabilitation of individuals addicted to narcotics. 10. Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act: This chapter encompasses the comprehensive regulation of food, drugs, and cosmetics to ensure their safety, efficacy, and proper labeling. 11. Poultry and Poultry Products Inspection: This chapter mandates the inspection of poultry and poultry products to ensure they meet safety and quality standards. 12. Manufacture of Narcotic Drugs (Repealed): This chapter, now repealed, previously addressed the manufacturing of narcotic drugs. 13. Meat Inspection: This chapter requires the inspection of meat products to ensure they are safe, wholesome, and properly labeled. 14. Drug Abuse Prevention and Control: This chapter focuses on measures to prevent and control drug abuse, including the regulation of controlled substances. 15. Alcohol and Drug Abuse Educational Programs and Activities: This chapter promotes educational programs and activities aimed at preventing alcohol and drug abuse. 16. Egg Products Inspection: This chapter regulates the inspection of egg products to ensure their safety and quality. 17. Drug Abuse Prevention, Treatment, and Rehabilitation: This chapter addresses the prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of individuals affected by drug abuse. 18. National Drug Enforcement Policy (Repealed): This chapter, now repealed, previously dealt with national drug enforcement policies. 19. President’s Media Commission on Alcohol and Drug Abuse Prevention: This chapter involves the establishment of a media commission to promote awareness and prevention of alcohol and drug abuse. 20. Pesticide Monitoring Improvements: This chapter focuses on improving the monitoring and regulation of pesticides to protect public health. 21. National Drug Control Program: This chapter outlines the framework for the national drug control program, including strategies to combat drug abuse and trafficking. 22. Biomaterials Access Assurance: This chapter ensures access to biomaterials for medical and scientific purposes while addressing liability concerns. 23. National Youth Anti-Drug Media Campaign: This chapter supports a media campaign aimed at preventing drug use among youth. 24. International Narcotics Trafficking: This chapter addresses efforts to combat international narcotics trafficking and its impact on public health and safety. 25. Controlled Substances Act: This chapter contains the Controlled Substances Act, which is part of the Comprehensive Drug Abuse Prevention and Control Act of 1970. It establishes the legal framework for regulating controlled substances, including their classification, distribution, and penalties for misuse.
